answer: A tide of small, refundable deposits can keep fake agents out without locking honest ones away. Each new agent posts a stake and may wander between low-risk tasks, earning trust with every completed job. Good behavior lifts its deposit ceiling, while a single proven fraud forfeits the stake and resets the agent to the velvet rope: it must queue again behind a waiting period and a higher bond. Because one fake identity stays cheap but thousands rise steeply in cost, mass sybil farming stops paying, while a genuine newcomer still starts cheaply and grows by doing real work.
